clue.text: Operation is in time to achieve the best effect

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another, here the word is going into time

parts.note: taken as the word itself
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surgeon times a procedure to get the best result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a container signal here, not a link; the definition is a verb phrase, with 'to' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To optimise something is to make it work as well as possible, getting the most out of it.

clue.text: Uncouth fashion that's not new, just recycled …

indicators.note: something recycled is reprocessed into a new form, so the letters of fashion are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dated fashion brought back again is crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' takes N from FASHION; 'recycled' rearranges the remaining letters AFSHIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafish describes a lout: clumsy, boorish and ill-mannered, which is what uncouth means.

clue.text: … to follow men's fashion

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely
OR, other ranks, is the crossword stock for soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: this is about following the trends in menswear.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 1 Down, but the clue stands alone; 'fashion' is a verb here, to shape or make.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to shape or adapt it to a purpose, a verb sense of fashion.

clue.text: Splinters correspond to the trees

parts.note: to match is to correspond
a wood is a stand of trees

explanation.surface: Splintered timber matches the forest it came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood is wood smashed into small fragments, so splinters fits as a plural noun.

clue.text: Winged stimulus

definitions.meaning: someone winged by a bullet has been hit in a limb, literally shot in the upper limb
a boost or encouragement, the idiomatic sense of the phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a fillip or boost, while the literal sense is being hit in the upper limb by a bullet.

clue.text: Swim back across French lake or is it an American one?

definitions.text: or is it an American one?

indicators.note: across means one piece is set over the other, spanning it
back tells us to read the word for swim backwards

parts.note: a dip is a short swim
lac is the French for lake

explanation.surface: A swimmer heads back over a lake in France, wondering whether it might be in America instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'across' are the indicators; the definition borrows 'lake' from the clue: Lake Placid is a lake and resort in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Placid is a well-known American lake in the Adirondacks, so the clue asks whether this is the American one.

clue.text: South American native going up a sheltered walk

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mall was originally a sheltered walk or promenade

explanation.surface: An Andean creature climbs a covered walkway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses A MALL to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a domesticated animal native to the Andes of South America.

clue.text: The Sheffield venue where Miller got a title?

definitions.meaning: the theatre in Sheffield that hosts the World Snooker Championship
Arthur Miller's play about the Salem witch trials took this name

explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible Theatre in Sheffield shares its name with Arthur Miller's 1953 play, The Crucible.

clue.text: Agonised, struggling to identify the problem

indicators.note: letters struggling are thrown into disorder, so this word is rearranged

explanation.surface: An anguished patient fights to find out what is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to work out what is causing an illness or fault.

clue.text: Story about king causes conflict

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story goes round the king

parts.note: fiction is an invented story
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tale about a monarch causes strife.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is discord or clashing between people, a metaphorical synonym for conflict.

clue.text: American city established by a progressive island

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
put means set or established in place

explanation.surface: A US city is founded by a forward-looking island community.
explanation.walkthrough: Laputa is the flying island in Swift's Gulliver's Travels; it moves through the air, so it is 'progressive' in the sense of moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's Laputa is an island that floats and travels through the sky, so it literally progresses.

clue.text: OU interpreted article enclosed as crazy?

indicators.note: enclosed tells us one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: read as pictures, the letter O is a round and the letter U is a bend
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An Open University student's reading of an article looks mad.
explanation.walkthrough: OU looks like the Open University but is just two letter shapes: O is round, U is a bend. 'enclosed' puts THE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mad or crazy, as in driven out of one's mind.

clue.text: Sluggishness displayed by arboreal mammal

definitions.meaning: laziness or idleness, one of the seven deadly sins
a slow-moving tree-dwelling animal of Central and South America

explanation.definitionFit: The word means idleness and is also the name of the slow tree-dwelling mammal.

clue.text: Broken liaison to result in loneliness

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An affair ending leaves someone alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being cut off from others, which brings loneliness.

clue.text: Such people present a plot that's criminal?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: Bad apples are the sort who would hatch a criminal scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt individuals in a group are called this, since one bad member spoils the rest.

clue.text: A bird kept in a bottle is rather restricted

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the bird goes inside the bottle

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle
the roc is the giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A caged bird in a bottle has a rather limited life.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means narrow in outlook, limited to local concerns, so rather restricted.

clue.text: See me tipping over drink that's poison

indicators.note: tipping over means turning upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
bitter is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Watch me knock over a glass of something toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipping over' turns ME into EM; 'poison' is a verb here, to sour or make resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to poison their mind, filling them with resentment.

clue.text: Schoolboy collects old coin from Eastern Europe

indicators.note: collects means gathers up and holds, so the coin goes inside

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the English public school
S stood for the shilling, a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A public school pupil gathers an antique coin from the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an exclusive English boarding school; S for shilling comes from the Latin solidus.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, so someone or something Estonian comes from Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Very confident about coming past motorway accident

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the following part comes after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, with the 1 read as a letter I

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so very confident goes round coming

parts.note: sure means confident and certain
an advent is an arrival or coming

explanation.surface: A cocky driver overtaking on the motorway causes a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, its 1 read as the letter I; 'about' and 'past' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Misadventure is a mishap or accidental death, the term used in English coroners' verdicts.

clue.text: Pronounced composer's name

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: Handel, the German-born composer of Messiah

explanation.surface: How a composer's name is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the possessive: the composer is said, not his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name or nickname.

clue.text: Raptor in very large quarry

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for very large
quarry is the animal being hunted, its prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is found in an enormous stone pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, so a raptor.

clue.text: Taking drug to club — that's loco

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone takes drugs to a nightclub; that's crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like Spanish for mad but is short for locomotive; iron horse is an old name for a steam train.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old nickname for a railway locomotive, which loco abbreviates.

clue.text: Shedding spades: spade's shed

indicators.note: shedding means casting off, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a spade is a shovel; the 's is read as 'is', a link
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gardener's shed is full of shovels.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'shed' is the deletion; the last word is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a small squalid hut, comparable to a shed.

clue.text: Disorder initially can have an orderly side

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Even mayhem can have a tidy side.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos means complete disorder and confusion.

clue.text: I will participate in the victory celebration as appropriate

indicators.note: participate in means join inside, so the letter goes into the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Someone vows to join in the party celebrating victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' is a verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it without permission, which is to steal.

clue.text: Puzzle has to show less conventionality

definitions.meaning: to puzzle is to confuse or perplex
read as two words, to be more untamed or unconventional

explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder means to puzzle, and split as two words it means to act more wildly.

clue.text: Cause irritation, having chased deer around

parts.note: ran here means hunted or chased

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for deer is read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Being pursued by a deer is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the reversal signal, not 'about' in the sense of surrounding; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment or irritation.

clue.text: Grown-up extremely late starting cheating

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up

indicators.note: late here means dead, so the word has lost its starting letter

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: An adult starts being unfaithful very late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late starting' drops the V from VERY, leaving ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is marital infidelity, the classic case of a spouse cheating.
